about.title: San Dimas Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Dimas recorded 3 traffic deaths in the most recent full year, alongside 139 injury collisions on roads like SR-57, SR-210, and Arrow Highway. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. If no immediate family exists, other dependents or heirs may have standing. These cases are separate from any criminal charges that might follow a fatal crash, and they exist to address the financial and emotional toll left behind, not to punish. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families in San Dimas with an independent attorney who can walk through what happened, who may be liable, and what the claim process looks like. There's no cost to start that conversation, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why San Dimas Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, usually a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible if none exist. An independent attorney can help determine where your family fits.

items.title: The Clock Starts Quickly
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a public roadway agency, may share fault. Waiting even a few months can matter.

items.title: Civil and Criminal Paths Are Separate
items.desc: A wrongful death claim proceeds independently of any criminal case tied to the crash. Even if charges are filed, delayed, or never brought, your family may still pursue a civil claim for damages.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have priority to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs, such as parents or siblings in certain situations, may have standing. An independent attorney can review your specific family situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a freeway like SR-57 or SR-210 instead of a city street?
items.answer: It can. If a state highway or Caltrans-maintained road is involved, or if a government vehicle was part of the crash, there may be a shorter filing deadline and additional notice requirements. This is one reason it helps to talk with an attorney early rather than waiting.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually recover for our family?
items.answer: California law allows recovery for tangible losses like funeral costs and the financial support the person would have provided, as well as intangible losses like the loss of their companionship and guidance. Every family's circumstances are different, so the value of a claim depends on the specific facts involved. No outcome can ever be guaranteed.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney; there's no charge to have that initial conversation. If an attorney takes your case, they typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your family recovers compensation.
